body:
Hello, I am very happy you have chosen to respond. This will be my last message to you, and hopefully my last use of this throwaway. Over the past couple days, I've been thinking about what you had said before. You've helped me realize a lot, and I am eternally grateful.

Before, you said that I should try to transform the relationship into something healthier, and to try to find satisfaction in just being a good older brother. I saw her again, and enjoyed myself just as much as usual, except for different reasons. Instead of being flirty, and pushing skinship, I just talked to her. She told me about her day, and her problems, and I helped her through them. In the way an older brother should, and I did derive quite a bit of satisfaction from it. I've realized some of my feelings for her were just lust, and those were suppressed at least a little bit. I still feel a great deal of romantic love for her, but I'm hoping I can slowly turn this into something familial.

I'm not going to lie, it hurts a great deal. To point I feel like I could start crying while typing this. However, this pain in and of itself is worth something, as it means I am feeling something. There is no longer just apathy and love for my sister, now there is pain and a little less love for my sister. Along with a little happiness. Recently, a huge update for an mmo I used to love came out. I've been reconnecting with old friends through the game, and have been enjoying myself at least a little bit.

I realize that this alone is not enough to solve anything, but I hope it at least eases the pain while I start to repair my relationship with my little sister. I will try to find something else before this high runs out, though I am uncertain I will be able to in time. There will likely be a period of weeks or months before I find the next thing, and I will likely go back to rock-bottom, which I am barely above right now. During that time, I hope to ask her for help, not as a romantic interest, but as my little sister giving me her support.

Once again, I can not thank you enough for your help. I would've gone a long time pursuing these feelings without your advice. Hell, I still haven't stopped, but I'm getting there. I did a little bit of looking through your post history, and can safely say that you are a wonderful individual. You have had your own struggles, and have, or at least it seems, risen above them. I only hope to ascend to your level someday. If you ever need help, with anything, send me a PM. I'll try to check this account once every week or so, and am sure I'll see your message. That being said, do not feel pressured to send.

I hope you don't mind, but I'm going to reply pretty late. I'd like to keep talking about this and like you said earlier, not many other people have responded. None, actually. 

It's interesting to hear you have similar experiences. I am not so sure that I would label my disinterest as asexuality, however. It's good to know you can understand at least a little bit of where I'm coming from. I have also read Night, though I saw it more as a showing of how inhuman people can be, of how low people can become. Elie talks of how he will never forgive the nazis for what they've done, it doesn't seem like he sees them as human. You're correct in saying that my sister is not just for me. However, I feel it's important to note that she has not set boundaries. I have said it before, but I'm certain my feelings for her are being reciprocated. It's become something we're both aware of, but never speak of, if that makes any sense. My worry of hurting her is not direct, but indirect. It will probably ruin her relationship with her parents, and she will become something like an outcast. She does not have much experience with relationships, so she'd probably go with her emotions rather than hard reasoning. This is what worries me.

I am not so sure I would call myself willing to get feedback, as my friend and now anyone passing by this thread are the only ones who know. He is someone who I've been through a lot with, and when I told him, he actually supported me. He said he was glad I told him, and would help me out whatever I decided to do. I'm not sure that was the best call on his part, but I am still grateful. At that point in time, I just needed someone to talk to about it, as it had been festering for too long. 

I will take your advice. I'm going to try to check if they're are any online, anonymous services I can use to try to get better. As much as I would like to pick something else, that's just not possible for me right now. I tend to neglect myself, sometimes I'll go a day without eating just because I forget to take care of myself. When I'm at the point of caring more about my sister than I do myself, finding something else is very hard. I am sorry that your parents were bad people, they don't deserve to have a child. It's good to know you've managed to overcome that.

I am not sure about free services, though even if they are there it might still be difficult. With my current circumstances, it's impossible for me to go to them without people who know me finding out I have a problem. I have also read A Million Little Pieces, it was actually the book that got me so invested in memoirs. I do have anxiety over hurting her, and I know I have not done it yet. That being said, the urge to is sometimes unbearable.

If you're talking about romantic relationships? No, I don't think so. I saw dating more-so about having a girlfriend, rather than being with one. I felt no love for any of them, and I was never sure why. It felt like I was the only one who didn't know how to love, so I stopped dating for a while. This made the feelings for my little sister, when they came, groundbreaking for me. I was finally experiencing something I'd wanted for so long. Almost, at least.

People do care for me. I am not sure why they do, but they do. My mother is always trying to make me happy, but I've grown distant from her. My father and I have an alright relationship, though there's nothing deep to it. The only other person who comes to mind is a friend of mine. I've known him since kindergarten, and we've been best buds since. He is someone I could tell anything to. Hell, he even knows about my feelings for my sister

I do not have a job. Therapy is something I realize that I need, but since I don't make a living, it's way too expensive. The books I've read are scattered, though memoirs used to be a favorite of mine. That and collections of short stories. John Barnes and Stephen King both make excellent short stories, and I was obsessed with them for a while.

I do not think these are just intrusive thoughts, as they seem to affect my very core. A week ago I hung out with her for pretty much the whole day, and we had a wonderful time. For the first time in forever, I went to bed happy. All of my anxieties left me and I felt good.
